messages:
anna-customer: Hey team — our Dedicated tenant acct-987 is seeing a big uptick in 429s and tail latency since ~09:12 UTC. Impacting billing webhooks and a few user-facing endpoints. Can someone take a look?

mike-support: Sorry you're hitting this, anna. Can you paste a sample request id and model/variant + approx seq len? Also which dedicated pool name?

anna-customer: req=01FZ9Q2A3, model=gpt-redwood-16k, variant=fp16, pool=dedi-east-2. We started a batch of long-context invoice-parsing jobs — many > 12k tokens. 429s spike at 09:12, sustained ~15m.

mike-support: Thanks. I pulled infra logs for dedi-east-2 around that window. Seeing a lot of kvcache evict messages + throttle enforcement on tenant acct-987. Short log clip: ```[09:12:08] kvcache_evict tenant=acct-987 freed_bytes=328M entries=420 reason=memory_pressure
[09:12:10] throttle enforcer tenant=acct-987 code=429 action=reject active_requests=240
[09:12:11] kvcache_eviction_ramp tenant=acct-987 frag_ratio=0.72
```

sara-engineering: My initial read — this looks like a capacity misprediction by autoscaler: the pool had scaled down overnight (low avg qps) and when the long-context batch hit, KV working set grew quickly causing fragmentation and large evictions. Eviction churn led to sustained latency and our throttle policy kicked in.

raj-eng-sre: Can you share a repro? If we can replay we should test an immediate mitigation (temporary move to burst pool or bump reserved slots). Also need heap/kv metrics + pprof of an affected node to confirm fragmentation pattern.

anna-customer: Repro steps (what we ran):
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json 
where payload.json contains a single prompt with ~13k tokens of document context and max_tokens=2048.
2) Run 40 concurrent requests with keep-alive for 10 minutes.
(We can share the exact payloads privately.)

mike-support: I've attached pointers to relevant traces (trace ids: trace-7f3, trace-7f4) and added acct-987 to a temporary higher-rate quota while we investigate. That should reduce immediate 429s.

infra-bot: ALERT: kvcache_pressure:dedi-east-2 node=n2-high-12 memory_used=92% threshold=85%

sara-engineering: Plan: (a) reproduce on staging with similar concurrency + long contexts, (b) capture pprof and kv-slab histograms, (c) exercise fallback routing to quantized-variant to see if reduced working set helps. Short-term: move acct-987 to burst pool or increase reserved capacity for 1 hour.

raj-eng-sre: +1. Also let's tweak the eviction backoff config for that pool to prefer graceful degradation (serve slower rather than instant mass eviction) — I can open a controlled rollout to one node.

anna-customer: Moving to burst pool helped immediately — 429s dropped after ~90s. Thanks. I'll keep load on for repro if you need it.

mike-support: Can you keep one failing request id handy if you reproduce? Also share full timestamps, and whether requests are using streaming. That helps root cause.

anna-customer: Will do. They use streaming with chunked responses. I'll upload exact sample and enable traces for the next run.

raj-eng-sre: Thx — assigning follow-up to oncall: @raj-eng-sre. We'll run mem/pprof capture and check slab fragmentation. If confirmed, follow-up actions: increase per-tenant slab quota, add admission control for excessively large KV growth, and add autoscaler config guard to avoid scaling below min_nodes when long-context signals present.

mike-support: Filed ticket SUP-8742, linked traces, added temporary quota bump, and noted mitigation steps. tagging eng-runbook:eng-runtime and eng-sre.

anna-customer: Appreciate the quick response. We'll gather repro payload and keep you posted. :thumbsup:

sara-engineering: Adding one more mitigation idea — client-side suggestion: chunk long contexts into smaller prefix caches (we can share a snippet) which reduces peak KV footprint.

anna-customer: Interested — please share snippet when you have it.

mike-support: Closing immediate incident thread but keeping ticket open until postmortem.

raj-eng-sre: Scheduling postmortem if ticket still open after 48h and will include recommendations for autoscale thresholds and eviction policy changes.

anna-customer: Thanks all.
